content.title: About
content.content: Mixed nuts without peanuts is a blend of selected nuts (almonds, cashews, hazelnuts, walnuts, pine nuts, etc.) lightly salted. The product contains no peanuts, making it safe for people with peanut allergy. The nuts retain their natural aroma and crunchy texture, while a hint of salt enhances their flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nut mixes are often used in cooking to add texture and flavor to dishes.
The absence of peanuts makes the blend suitable for most diets, including gluten‑free and dairy‑free.
The salt used is usually sea salt, adding trace minerals such as magnesium and iodine.
Nuts in the mix may be roasted separately before being combined to preserve their individual taste notes.
Mixed nuts are a popular snack paired with wine or beer.

items.title: Rich in healthy fats
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: The blend provides a substantial amount of protein useful for muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is a powerful antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High in minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, phosphorus, zinc and iron, important for metabolism and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber in nuts promotes regular bowel function and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Even without peanuts, the mix can trigger reactions in people allergic to any of the included nuts.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Nuts are calorie‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Individuals monitoring sodium intake should consider the amount of added salt.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Whole nuts can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The mixed nuts can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, muesli, baked goods, or used in sauces. For extra aroma, nuts can be briefly toasted in a dry pan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the mix in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard nuts that smell rancid or have off‑flavors.
